description: Hybrid connectivity. VPC A has a virtual private gateway with a Site-to-Site VPN whose static route is 192.168.0.0/16; VPC B reaches on-premises through a transit gateway with a VPN attachment (10.50.0.0/16, learned by BGP) and a Direct Connect gateway attachment (172.16.0.0/12). A connection from on-premises works only when it arrives over a link, passes the network ACLs and security group as the client's own address, and the server's subnet routes the replies back over the same link: the database's subnet has no route on-premises, so nothing there can reach it directly; but an on-premises host that takes over the app server over SSH reaches the database from there, which the attack chains from on-premises show. A network ACL denies RDP from the Direct Connect range. Outbound, servers reach on-premises over the same links, and the replies must come back to their subnet.
